newsitem.title: USA: US FCC chief lists long-distance points for Bells.
newsitem.headline: US FCC chief lists long-distance points for Bells.

text.p: The head of the U.S. Federal Communications Commission Wednesday spelled out some of the conditions his agency will use when judging whether to allow a Baby Bell phone company into the long-distance business.

Under the recent communications act, the Bells can enter the long distance business once they have opened their local markets to long-distance carriers, cable-TV operators and other new entrants to the local phone business.
FCC Chairman Reed Hundt told a meeting of state regulators in San Francisco that one question will dominate his agency's consideration of all Bell long-distance requests.
"Do the conditions established, through arbitration agreements and other rules, give all parties a fair opportunity to compete in the local market?" he said.
A copy of the speech was released in Washington.
State regulators currently are issuing arbitration decisions governing the terms and conditions under which long-distance carriers and others can hook up to the local phone network.

The regulators have been given the added responsibility of determining the price at which the linkups occur because key provisions of the FCC's "interconnection" order were suspended last month by a U.S. appeals court.
Hundt said that among the other factors the FCC will examine when considering the Bell requests include:
-- Are individual, or "unbundled," elements of the the Bell's local networks available to new entrants at competitive prices based on the cost of new and more efficient facilities?
-- Are transport and termination available at cost-based rates?
-- Can whole local networks be leased at retail rates, less costs that could be avoided?
-- Have articifical barriers to competition been removed?
-- Can consumers and businesses easily take their local phone number with them if they choose to switch carriers?
The Bell long-distance requests are expected to start coming to the FCC next year.
